7669 — Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said to Ka‘b ibn ‘Ujrah: “May God protect you from the leadership of foolish people.” He said: “What is the leadership of foolish people?” He said: “Leaders who will come after me; they will not follow my guidance and will not act according to my way. Whoever believes them in their lies and helps them in their oppression, they are not from me and I am not from them, and they will not come to my reservoir. Whoever does not believe them in their lies and does not help them in their oppression, they are from me and I am from them, and they will come to my reservoir. Ka‘b ibn ‘Ujrah, fasting is a shield, charity extinguishes sin, and prayer is nearness — or he said: proof. Ka‘b ibn ‘Ujrah, no flesh that grows from unlawful earnings will enter Paradise; the Fire is more deserving of it. Ka‘b ibn ‘Ujrah, people go out in two ways: one buys himself and frees himself, and another sells himself and destroys himself.”
 Fair: Narrated by Ahmad (14441) and ‘Abd al-Razzaq (20719).

٧٦٦٩ — عن جابر بن عبد الله أن النبي ﷺ قال لكعب بن عجرة: ((أعاذك الله من إمارة السفهاء)). قال: وما إمارة السفهاء؟ قال: ((أمراء يكونون بعدي، لا يقتدون بهديي، ولا يستنون بسنتي، فمن صدقهم بكذبهم، وأعانهم على ظلمهم، فأولئك ليسوا مني ولست منهم، ولا يردون علي حوضي. ومن لم يصدقهم بكذبهم، ولم يعنهم على ظلمهم، فأولئك مني وأنا منهم، وسيردون علي حوضي. يا كعب بن عجرة، الصوم جنة، والصدقة تطفئ الخطيئة، والصلاة قربان — أو قال: برهان — يا كعب بن عجرة، إنه لا يدخل الجنة لحم نبت من سحت، النار أولى به. يا كعب بن عجرة، الناس غاديان: فمبتاع نفسه فمعتقها، وبائع نفسه فموبقها)).
 حسن: رواه أحمد (١٤٤٤١)، وعبد الرزاق (٢٠٧١٩).
7669 — Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said to Ka‘b ibn ‘Ujrah: “May God protect you from the leadership of foolish people.” He said: “What is the leadership of foolish people?” He said: “Leaders who will come after me; they will not follow my guidance and will not act according to my way. Whoever believes them in their lies and helps them in their oppression, they are not from me and I am not from them, and they will not come to my reservoir. Whoever does not believe them in their lies and does not help them in their oppression, they are from me and I am from them, and they will come to my reservoir. Ka‘b ibn ‘Ujrah, fasting is a shield, charity extinguishes sin, and prayer is nearness — or he said: proof. Ka‘b ibn ‘Ujrah, no flesh that grows from unlawful earnings will enter Paradise; the Fire is more deserving of it. Ka‘b ibn ‘Ujrah, people go out in two ways: one buys himself and frees himself, and another sells himself and destroys himself.”
 Fair: Narrated by Ahmad (14441) and ‘Abd al-Razzaq (20719).

٧٦٧١ — عن حذيفة بن اليمان قال: كان الناس يسألون رسول الله ﷺ عن الخير، وكنت أسأل عن الشر مخافة أن يدركني، فقلت: يا رسول الله، إنا كنا في جاهلية وشر، فجاءنا الله بهذا الخير، فهل بعد هذا الخير من شر؟ قال: ((نعم)). قلت: وهل بعد ذلك الشر من خير؟ قال: ((نعم، وفيه دَخَن)). قلت: وما دَخَنُه؟ قال: ((قوم يهدون بغير هديي، تعرف منهم وتنكر)). قلت: فهل بعد ذلك الخير من شر؟ قال: ((نعم، دعاة على أبواب جهنم، من أجابهم إليها قذفوه فيها)). قلت: يا رسول الله، صفهم لنا. قال: ((هم من جلدتنا، ويتكلمون بألسنتنا)). قلت: فما تأمرني إن أدركني ذلك؟ قال: ((تلزم جماعة المسلمين وإمامهم)). قلت: فإن لم يكن لهم جماعة ولا إمام؟ قال: ((فاعتزل تلك الفرق كلها، ولو أن تعض بأصل شجرة حتى يدركك الموت، وأنت على ذلك)).
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٧٠٨٤)، ومسلم (١٨٤٧).
 وقوله في الحديث: “تلزم جماعة المسلمين” قال الطبري: “أي الذين في طاعة من اجتمعوا على تأميره، فمن نكث بيعته خرج عن الجماعة. قال: وفي الحديث أنه متى لم يكن للناس إمام، فافترق الناس أحزابًا، فلا يتبع أحدًا في الفرقة، ويعتزل الجميع إن استطاع ذلك خشية من الوقوع في الشر”. انظر: فتح الباري (٣٧/١٠).

7671 — Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman said: People used to ask the Messenger of God ﷺ about good, while I used to ask him about evil, fearing that it might reach me. I said: “Messenger of God, we were in ignorance and evil, then God brought us this good. Will there be evil after this good?” He said: “Yes.” I said: “Will there be good after that evil?” He said: “Yes, but in it there will be impurity.” I said: “What is its impurity?” He said: “People who guide by other than my guidance; you will recognize some of what they do and reject some.” I said: “Will there be evil after that good?” He said: “Yes, callers at the gates of Hell; whoever responds to them, they will throw him into it.” I said: “Messenger of God, describe them to us.” He said: “They are from our own people and speak our language.” I said: “What do you command me to do if that reaches me?” He said: “Adhere to the community of Muslims and their leader.” I said: “What if they have no community and no leader?” He said: “Then withdraw from all those groups, even if you must bite onto the root of a tree until death reaches you while you are upon that.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (7084) and Muslim (1847).
 His statement in the hadith, “Adhere to the community of Muslims,” al-Tabari said: “Meaning those who are in obedience to the one whom they have collectively appointed as leader. Whoever breaks his pledge has left the community.” He said: “In the hadith is that whenever people have no leader and split into factions, one should not follow anyone into division, and should withdraw from all of them if able, out of fear of falling into evil.” See Fath al-Bari (10/37).

 وقوله في الحديث: “تلزم جماعة المسلمين” قال الطبري: “أي الذين في طاعة من اجتمعوا على تأميره، فمن نكث بيعته خرج عن الجماعة. قال: وفي الحديث أنه متى لم يكن للناس إمام، فافترق الناس أحزابًا، فلا يتبع أحدًا في الفرقة، ويعتزل الجميع إن استطاع ذلك خشية من الوقوع في الشر”. انظر: فتح الباري (٣٧/١٠).
7671 — Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman said: People used to ask the Messenger of God ﷺ about good, while I used to ask him about evil, fearing that it might reach me. I said: “Messenger of God, we were in ignorance and evil, then God brought us this good. Will there be evil after this good?” He said: “Yes.” I said: “Will there be good after that evil?” He said: “Yes, but in it there will be impurity.” I said: “What is its impurity?” He said: “People who guide by other than my guidance; you will recognize some of what they do and reject some.” I said: “Will there be evil after that good?” He said: “Yes, callers at the gates of Hell; whoever responds to them, they will throw him into it.” I said: “Messenger of God, describe them to us.” He said: “They are from our own people and speak our language.” I said: “What do you command me to do if that reaches me?” He said: “Adhere to the community of Muslims and their leader.” I said: “What if they have no community and no leader?” He said: “Then withdraw from all those groups, even if you must bite onto the root of a tree until death reaches you while you are upon that.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (7084) and Muslim (1847).
 His statement in the hadith, “Adhere to the community of Muslims,” al-Tabari said: “Meaning those who are in obedience to the one whom they have collectively appointed as leader. Whoever breaks his pledge has left the community.” He said: “In the hadith is that whenever people have no leader and split into factions, one should not follow anyone into division, and should withdraw from all of them if able, out of fear of falling into evil.” See Fath al-Bari (10/37).

7673 — Ibn ‘Umar said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said to us: “Religion is sincere counsel.” He said: We said: “For whom, Messenger of God?” He said: “For God, His Messenger, His Book, the leaders of the Muslims, and their common people.”
 Fair: Narrated by al-Bazzar — Kashf al-Astar (62), al-Darimi (2796), and al-Tahawi in Sharh al-Mushkil (1447).
The meaning of sincere counsel for God, Glorified is He, is sound belief in His oneness and sincerity of intention in worshiping Him. Sincere counsel for the Book of God is to believe in it and act according to what is in it. Sincere counsel for His Messenger is to affirm his prophethood and give obedience to him in what he commanded and forbade. Sincere counsel for the leaders of the Muslims is to obey them in truth and not to consider revolt against them with the sword if they are unjust. Sincere counsel for the general Muslims is to guide them to what benefits them. This was mentioned by al-Khattabi in Ma‘alim al-Sunan.

7674 — Zayd ibn Thabit said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “There are three qualities over which the heart of a Muslim will never harbor rancor: making deeds sincere for God, sincerely advising those in authority, and adhering to the community; for their supplication surrounds those behind them.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Ahmad (21590), and graded authentic by Ibn Hibban (67).

٧٦٧٥ — عن شريح بن عبيد الحضرمي، وغيره، قال: جلد عياض بن غنم صاحبَ دارا حين فُتحت، فأغلظ له هشام بن حكيم القول حتى غضب عياض، ثم مكث ليالي، فأتاه هشام بن حكيم فاعتذر إليه، ثم قال هشام لعياض: ألم تسمع النبي ﷺ يقول: ((إن من أشد الناس عذابًا أشدهم عذابًا في الدنيا للناس))؟ فقال عياض بن غنم: يا هشام بن حكيم، قد سمعنا ما سمعت، ورأينا ما رأيت، أو لم تسمع رسول الله ﷺ يقول: ((من أراد أن ينصح لسلطان بأمر، فلا يبد له علانية، ولكن ليأخذ بيده فيخلو به، فإن قبل منه فذاك، وإلا كان قد أدى الذي عليه له))، وإنك يا هشام لأنت الجريء، إذ تجترئ على سلطان الله، فهلا خشيت أن يقتلك السلطان، فتكون قتيل سلطان الله تبارك وتعالى؟
 حسن: رواه أحمد (١٥٣٣٣).
ومنهج أهل السنة والجماعة مناصحة ولاة الأمور سرًا، ولا يكون ذلك على المنابر والمجامع.
 فقد كان الصحابة ينصحون الولاة سرًا، وقد قيل لأسامة بن زيد: ما يمنعك أن تدخل على عثمان، فتكلمه فيما يصنع؟ فقال أسامة: إنكم لترون أني لا أكلمه إلا أسمعكم، إني أكلمه في السر دون أن أفتح بابًا لا أكون أول من فتحه. رواه البخاري (٣٢٦٧)، ومسلم (٢٩٨٩).
قال سماحة الشيخ عبد العزيز بن باز رحمه الله تعالى: “ليس من منهج السلف التشهير بعيوب الولاة، وذكر ذلك على المنابر؛ لأن ذلك يفضي إلى الانقلابات، وعدم السمع والطاعة في المعروف، ويفضي إلى الخروج الذي يضر ولا ينفع. ولكن الطريقة المتبعة عند السلف النصيحة فيما بينهم وبين السلطان، والكتابة إليه، أو الاتصال بالعلماء الذين يتصلون به حتى يوجه إلى الخير”. حقوق الراعي والرعية (ص ٢٧-٢٨)، فتوى الشيخ في آخر الرسالة المذكورة.

7675 — Shurayh ibn ‘Ubayd al-Hadrami and others said: ‘Iyad ibn Ghanm flogged the governor of Dara when it was conquered, so Hisham ibn Hakim spoke harshly to him until ‘Iyad became angry. Then some nights passed, and Hisham ibn Hakim came to him and apologized to him. ٧٦٧٥ — عن شريح بن عبيد الحضرمي، وغيره، قال: جلد عياض بن غنم صاحبَ دارا حين فُتحت، فأغلظ له هشام بن حكيم القول حتى غضب عياض، ثم مكث ليالي، فأتاه هشام بن حكيم فاعتذر إليه، ثم قال هشام لعياض: ألم تسمع النبي ﷺ يقول: ((إن من أشد الناس عذابًا أشدهم عذابًا في الدنيا للناس))؟ فقال عياض بن غنم: يا هشام بن حكيم، قد سمعنا ما سمعت، ورأينا ما رأيت، أو لم تسمع رسول الله ﷺ يقول: ((من أراد أن ينصح لسلطان بأمر، فلا يبد له علانية، ولكن ليأخذ بيده فيخلو به، فإن قبل منه فذاك، وإلا كان قد أدى الذي عليه له))، وإنك يا هشام لأنت الجريء، إذ تجترئ على سلطان الله، فهلا خشيت أن يقتلك السلطان، فتكون قتيل سلطان الله تبارك وتعالى؟
 حسن: رواه أحمد (١٥٣٣٣).
ومنهج أهل السنة والجماعة مناصحة ولاة الأمور سرًا، ولا يكون ذلك على المنابر والمجامع.

٧٦٧٦ — عن عَرْفَجَة قال: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول:
«إِنَّهُ سَتَكُونُ هَنَاتٌ وَهَنَاتٌ، فَمَنْ أَرَادَ أَنْ يُفَرِّقَ أَمْرَ هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةِ وَهِيَ جَمِيعٌ، فَاضْرِبُوهُ بِالسَّيْفِ كَائِنًا مَنْ كَانَ».
وفي لفظ:
رأيت النبي ﷺ وهو على المنبر يخطب الناس، فقال:
«إِنَّهُ سَيَكُونُ بَعْدِي هَنَاتٌ وَهَنَاتٌ، فَمَنْ رَأَيْتُمُوهُ فَارَقَ الْجَمَاعَةَ، أَوْ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يُفَرِّقَ أَمْرَ أُمَّةِ مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ كَائِنًا مَنْ كَانَ، فَاقْتُلُوهُ؛ فَإِنَّ يَدَ اللَّهِ عَلَى الْجَمَاعَةِ، فَإِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ مَعَ مَنْ فَارَقَ الْجَمَاعَةَ يَرْكُضُ».
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٨٥٢)، واللفظ الثاني رواه النسائي (٤٠٢٠)، وصححه ابن حبان (٤٥٧٧).
وقوله: «هَنَات وهَنَات»: الهَنَات جمع هَنَة، وتطلق على كل شيء، والمراد بها الفتن والأمور الحادثة.

7676 — ʿArfajah reported:
I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
“There will be disturbances and troubles. Whoever seeks to divide the affairs of this Ummah while it is united, then strike him with the sword, whoever he may be.”
In another wording:
I saw the Prophet ﷺ while he was on the pulpit addressing the people, and he said:
“After me there will be disturbances and troubles. Whoever you see separating from the community, or seeking to divide the affairs of the Ummah of Muḥammad ﷺ, whoever he may be, then kill him. For the Hand of Allah is over the community, and Satan runs alongside the one who separates from the community.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1852). The second wording was narrated by al-Nasāʾī (4020) and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (4577).
The expression “hanāt and hanāt” uses the plural of hanah, a word that may refer generally to matters or occurrences; here it means trials, disturbances, and newly arising events.

“There will be disturbances and troubles. Whoever seeks to divide the affairs of this Ummah while it is united, then strike him with the sword, whoever he may be.”
In another wording:
I saw the Prophet ﷺ while he was on the pulpit addressing the people, and he said:
“After me there will be disturbances and troubles. Whoever you see separating from the community, or seeking to divide the affairs of the Ummah of Muḥammad ﷺ, whoever he may be, then kill him. For the Hand of Allah is over the community, and Satan runs alongside the one who separates from the community.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1852). The second wording was narrated by al-Nasāʾī (4020) and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (4577).
The expression “hanāt and hanāt” uses the plural of hanah, a word that may refer generally to matters or occurrences; here it means trials, disturbances, and newly arising events.

٧٦٧٧ — عن عبد الرحمن بن عبد رب الكعبة قال: دخلت المسجد، فإذا عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص جالس في ظل الكعبة، والناس مجتمعون عليه، فأتيتهم، فجلست إليه فقال: كنا مع رسول الله ﷺ في سفر، فنزلنا منزلًا، فمنا من يصلح خباءه، ومنا من ينتضل، ومنا من هو في جَشَرِه، إذ تنادى منادي رسول الله ﷺ: الصلاة جامعة. فاجتمعنا إلى رسول الله ﷺ فقال: ((إنه لم يكن نبي قبلي إلا كان حقًا عليه أن يدل أمته على خير ما يعلمه لهم، وينذرهم شر ما يعلمه لهم، وإن أمتكم هذه جُعلت عافيتها في أولها، وسيصيب آخرها بلاء، وأمور تنكرونها، وتجيء فتنة فيرقّق بعضها بعضًا، وتجيء الفتنة فيقول المؤمن: هذه مهلكتي، ثم تنكشف، وتجيء الفتنة فيقول المؤمن: هذه هذه. فمن أحب أن يُزحزح عن النار ويدخل الجنة، فلتأته منيته وهو يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر، وليأتِ إلى الناس الذي يحب أن يُؤتى إليه، ومن بايع إمامًا فأعطاه صفقة يده وثمرة قلبه، فليطعه إن استطاع، فإن جاء آخر ينازعه فاضربوا عنق الآخر)).
 فدنوت منه، فقلت له: أنشدك الله، آنت سمعت هذا من رسول الله ﷺ؟ فأهوى إلى أذنيه وقلبه بيديه، وقال: سمعته أذناي ووعاه قلبي. فقلت له: هذا ابن عمك معاوية يأمرنا أن نأكل أموالنا بيننا بالباطل، ونقتل أنفسنا، والله يقول: (يَٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا لَا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوَٰلَكُم بَيْنَكُم بِٱلْبَٰطِلِ إِلَّا أَن تَكُونَ تِجَٰرَةً عَن تَرَاضٍ مِّنكُمْ وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا أَنفُسَكُمْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِكُمْ رَحِيمًا) [النساء: ٢٩]. قال: فسكت ساعة، ثم قال: أطعه في طاعة الله، واعصه في معصية الله.
 صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٨٤٤:٤٦).

7677 — ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Abd Rabb al-Ka‘bah said: I entered the mosque and saw ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr ibn al-‘As sitting in the shade of the Ka‘bah, with people gathered around him. I came to them and sat with him, and he said: We were with the Messenger of God ﷺ on a journey, and we stopped at a place. Some of us were repairing their tents, some were practicing archery, and some were with their grazing animals, when the caller of the Messenger of God ﷺ called out: “The prayer is gathering.” So we gathered to the Messenger of God ﷺ, and he said: “There was no prophet before me except that it was a duty upon him to guide his nation to the best of what he knew for them, and to warn them of the worst of what he knew for them. The well-being of this nation of yours has been placed in its beginning, and its end will be struck by affliction and matters you will reject. A trial will come, and each one will make the one before it seem small. A trial will come and the believer will say: ‘This is my destruction,’ then it will be removed. Another trial will come and the believer will say: ‘This, this.’ So whoever loves to be moved away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise, let his death come to him while he believes in God and the Last Day, and let him treat people as he would love to be treated. Whoever pledges allegiance to a leader, giving him the clasp of his hand and the fruit of his heart, let him obey him if he is able. If another comes to dispute with him, strike the neck of the latter.”
 I came close to him and said: “I ask you by God, did you hear this from the Messenger of God ﷺ?” He pointed with his hands to his ears and his heart and said: “My ears heard it and my heart retained it.” I said to him: “This cousin of yours, Mu‘awiyah, commands us to consume our wealth among ourselves falsely and to kill ourselves, while God says: ‘O you who believe, do not consume your wealth among yourselves falsely, except that it be trade by mutual consent among you, and do not kill yourselves. Indeed, God is Merciful to you.’” [Women: 29] He remained silent for a while, then said: “Obey him in obedience to God, and disobey him in disobedience to God.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1844:46).

٧٦٧٩ — عن علي بن أبي طالب قال: إذا حدثتكم عن رسول الله ﷺ حديثًا، فوالله لأن أخرَّ من السماء أحب إليّ من أن أكذب عليه، وإذا حدثتكم فيما بيني وبينكم، فإن الحرب خَدعة. وإني سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول: ((سيخرج قوم في آخر الزمان أحداث الأسنان، سفهاء الأحلام، يقولون من خير قول البرية، لا يجاوز إيمانهم حناجرهم، يمرقون من الدين كما يمرق السهم من الرمية، فأينما لقيتموهم فاقتلوهم، فإن في قتلهم أجرًا لمن قتلهم يوم القيامة)).

٧٦٨٠ — عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: بينما النبي ﷺ يقسم، جاء عبد الله بن ذي الخويصرة التميمي فقال: اعدل يا رسول الله. فقال: ((ويلك، ومن يعدل إذا لم أعدل؟)). قال عمر بن الخطاب: دعني أضرب عنقه. قال: ((دعه، فإن له أصحابًا يحقر أحدكم صلاته مع صلاته، وصيامه مع صيامه، يمرقون من الدين كما يمرق السهم من الرمية، ينظر في قُذَذه فلا يوجد فيه شيء، ثم ينظر في نصله فلا يوجد فيه شيء، ثم ينظر في رِصافه فلا يوجد فيه شيء، ثم ينظر في نَضِيِّه فلا يوجد فيه شيء، قد سبق الفرث والدم. آيتهم رجل إحدى يديه — أو قال: ثدييه — مثل ثدي المرأة، أو قال: مثل البَضعة، تَدَرْدَر، يخرجون على حين فُرقة من الناس)).
 قال أبو سعيد: أشهد أني سمعت هذا من النبي ﷺ، وأشهد أن عليًا قتلهم وأنا معه، فجيء بالرجل على النعت الذي نعته النبي ﷺ. قال: فنزلت فيه: (وَمِنْهُم مَّن يَلْمِزُكَ فِي ٱلصَّدَقَٰتِ) [التوبة: ٥٨].
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٩٣٣)، ومسلم (١٠٦٤:١٤٨)، واللفظ للبخاري.

7680 — Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri said: While the Prophet ﷺ was distributing, ‘Abdullah ibn Dhi al-Khuwaysirah al-Tamimi came and said: “Be just, Messenger of God.” He said: “Woe to you! Who will be just if I am not just?” ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab said: “Let me strike his neck.” He said: “Leave him, for he will have companions. One of you would consider his prayer insignificant compared to their prayer, and his fasting compared to their fasting. They will pass out of the religion as an arrow passes through the prey. One looks at its feathers and finds nothing on them, then looks at its iron head and finds nothing on it, then looks at its binding and finds nothing on it, then looks at its shaft and finds nothing on it; it has passed through dung and blood. Their sign is a man whose one hand — or he said: one breast — is like a woman’s breast, or like a piece of flesh, moving loosely. They will emerge at a time of division among the people.”
 Abu Sa‘id said: I testify that I heard this from the Prophet ﷺ, and I testify that ‘Ali killed them while I was with him, and the man was brought according to the description that the Prophet ﷺ had given. He said: Then this was revealed about him: “And among them are those who criticize you concerning the charities.” [Repentance: 58]
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (6933) and Muslim (1064:148). The wording is from al-Bukhari.

7681 — Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri said: ‘Ali sent a small piece of gold to the Prophet ﷺ, so he distributed it among four people: al-Aqra‘ ibn Habis al-Hanzali, then al-Mujashi‘i; ‘Uyaynah ibn Badr al-Fazari; Zayd al-Ta’i, then one of Banu Nabhan; and ‘Alqamah ibn ‘Ulathah al-‘Amiri, then one of Banu Kilab. Quraysh and the Ansar became angry and said: “He gives to the chiefs of the people of Najd and leaves us!” He said: “I am only reconciling their hearts.” Then a man came forward with sunken eyes, prominent cheeks, a protruding forehead, a thick beard, and a shaved head. He said: “Fear God, Muhammad!” He said: “Who would obey God if I disobeyed Him? God has entrusted me over the people of the earth, yet you do not trust me?” A man asked permission to kill him — I think it was Khalid ibn al-Walid — but he prevented him. When the man turned away, he said: “From the offspring of this man, or from those who come after him, will be a people who recite the Quran but it will not pass beyond their throats. They will pass out of the religion as an arrow passes through the prey. They will kill the people of Islam and leave the people of idols. If I reach them, I will surely kill them with the killing of ‘Ad.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3344) and Muslim (1064:143).

٧٦٨١ — عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: بعث علي إلى النبي ﷺ بذُهَيْبة، فقسمها بين الأربعة: الأقرع بن حابس الحنظلي ثم المجاشعي، وعيينة بن بدر الفزاري، وزيد الطائي ثم أحد بني نبهان، وعلقمة بن علاثة العامري ثم أحد بني كلاب، فغضبت قريش والأنصار، قالوا: يعطي صناديد أهل نجد، ويدعنا! قال: ((إنما أتألفهم)). فأقبل رجل غائر العينين، مشرف الوجنتين، ناتئ الجبين، كثّ اللحية، محلوق، فقال: اتق الله يا محمد! فقال: ((من يطع الله إذا عصيت؟ أيأمنني الله على أهل الأرض فلا تأمنوني؟)). فسأله رجل قتله — أحسبه خالد بن الوليد — فمنعه. فلما ولى قال: ((إن من ضئضئ هذا، أو في عقب هذا، قومًا يقرؤون القرآن لا يجاوز حناجرهم، يمرقون من الدين مروق السهم من الرمية، يقتلون أهل الإسلام، ويدعون أهل الأوثان، لئن أنا أدركتهم لأقتلنهم قتل عاد)).
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٣٤٤)، ومسلم (١٠٦٤:١٤٣).
7681 — Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri said: ‘Ali sent a small piece of gold to the Prophet ﷺ, so he distributed it among four people: al-Aqra‘ ibn Habis al-Hanzali, then al-Mujashi‘i; ‘Uyaynah ibn Badr al-Fazari; Zayd al-Ta’i, then one of Banu Nabhan; and ‘Alqamah ibn ‘Ulathah al-‘Amiri, then one of Banu Kilab. Quraysh and the Ansar became angry and said: “He gives to the chiefs of the people of Najd and leaves us!” He said: “I am only reconciling their hearts.” Then a man came forward with sunken eyes, prominent cheeks, a protruding forehead, a thick beard, and a shaved head. He said: “Fear God, Muhammad!” He said: “Who would obey God if I disobeyed Him? God has entrusted me over the people of the earth, yet you do not trust me?” A man asked permission to kill him — I think it was Khalid ibn al-Walid — but he prevented him. When the man turned away, he said: “From the offspring of this man, or from those who come after him, will be a people who recite the Quran but it will not pass beyond their throats. They will pass out of the religion as an arrow passes through the prey. They will kill the people of Islam and leave the people of idols. If I reach them, I will surely kill them with the killing of ‘Ad.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3344) and Muslim (1064:143).

arabic_source:
٧٦٨٢ — عن زيد بن وهب الجهني أنه كان في الجيش الذين كانوا مع علي رضي الله عنه، الذين ساروا إلى الخوارج، فقال علي رضي الله عنه: أيها الناس، إني سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول: ((يخرج قوم من أمتي يقرؤون القرآن، ليس قراءتكم إلى قراءتهم بشيء، ولا صلاتكم إلى صلاتهم بشيء، ولا صيامكم إلى صيامهم بشيء، يقرؤون القرآن يحسبون أنه لهم وهو عليهم، لا تجاوز صلاتهم تراقيهم، يمرقون من الإسلام كما يمرق السهم من الرمية)).
 لو يعلم الجيش الذين يصيبونهم ما قُضي لهم على لسان نبيهم ﷺ لاتكلوا عن العمل. وآية ذلك أن فيهم رجلًا له عَضُد، وليس له ذراع، على رأس عضده مثل حلمة الثدي، عليه شعرات بيض. فتذهبون إلى معاوية وأهل الشام، وتتركون هؤلاء يخلفونكم في ذراريكم وأموالكم؟ والله إني لأرجو أن يكونوا هؤلاء القوم؛ فإنهم قد سفكوا الدم الحرام، وأغاروا في سرح الناس، فسيروا على اسم الله.
 قال سلمة بن كهيل: فنزلني زيد بن وهب منزلًا حتى قال: مررنا على قنطرة، فلما التقينا، وعلى الخوارج يومئذ عبد الله بن وهب الراسبي، فقال لهم: ألقوا الرماح، وسلوا سيوفكم من جفونها، فإني أخاف أن يناشدوكم كما ناشدوكم يوم حروراء. فرجعوا، فوَحَشُوا برماحهم، وسلّوا السيوف، وشجرهم الناس برماحهم. قال: وقُتل بعضهم على بعض، وما أصيب من الناس يومئذ إلا رجلان. فقال علي رضي الله عنه: التمسوا فيهم المُخْدَج. فالتمسوه، فلم يجدوه. فقام علي رضي الله عنه بنفسه حتى أتى ناسًا قد قُتل بعضهم على بعض، قال: أخّروهم. فوجدوه مما يلي الأرض، فكبر ثم قال: صدق الله، وبلغ رسوله. قال: فقام إليه عبيدة السلماني فقال: يا أمير المؤمنين، آلله الذي لا إله إلا هو، لسمعت هذا الحديث من رسول الله ﷺ؟ فقال: إي والله الذي لا إله إلا هو. حتى استحلفه ثلاثًا، وهو يحلف له.
 صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٠٦٦:١٥٦).

7682 — Zayd ibn Wahb al-Juhani was in the army that was with ‘Ali, may God be pleased with him, which marched against the Kharijites. ‘Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: “People, I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘A people will emerge from my nation who recite the Quran. Your recitation will be nothing compared to their recitation, your prayer will be nothing compared to their prayer, and your fasting will be nothing compared to their fasting. They recite the Quran thinking it is for them, while it is against them. Their prayer will not pass beyond their collarbones. They will pass out of Islam as an arrow passes through the prey.’
 If the army who strikes them knew what had been decreed for them upon the tongue of their Prophet ﷺ, they would rely upon that and abandon work. The sign of that is that among them is a man who has an upper arm but no forearm; at the end of his upper arm is something like the nipple of a breast, with white hairs upon it. Will you go to Mu‘awiyah and the people of Syria and leave these people behind you among your children and wealth? By God, I hope that these are those people, for they have shed inviolable blood and raided the people’s grazing animals. So march in the name of God.”
 Salamah ibn Kuhayl said: Zayd ibn Wahb described the places to me until he said: We passed over a bridge. When we met, the Kharijites that day were led by ‘Abdullah ibn Wahb al-Rasibi. He said to them: “Throw down the spears and draw your swords from their sheaths, for I fear that they will appeal to you as they appealed to you on the day of Harura’.” So they returned, cast aside their spears, and drew their swords. The people thrust at them with spears. He said: They were killed one upon another, and only two of the people were injured that day. ‘Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: “Search among them for the defective one.” They searched but did not find him. Then ‘Ali himself stood up and came to people who had been killed piled upon one another. He said: “Move them back.” They found him beneath them, so he proclaimed greatness and said: “God spoke the truth, and His Messenger conveyed.” Then ‘Ubaydah al-Salmani stood and said: “Commander of the believers, by God, besides whom there is no deity, did you truly hear this hadith from the Messenger of God ﷺ?” He said: “Yes, by God, besides whom there is no deity.” He made him swear three times, and he swore to him.
 Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1066:156).

 قال سلمة بن كهيل: فنزلني زيد بن وهب منزلًا حتى قال: مررنا على قنطرة، فلما التقينا، وعلى الخوارج يومئذ عبد الله بن وهب الراسبي، فقال لهم: ألقوا الرماح، وسلوا سيوفكم من جفونها، فإني أخاف أن يناشدوكم كما ناشدوكم يوم حروراء. فرجعوا، فوَحَشُوا برماحهم، وسلّوا السيوف، وشجرهم الناس برماحهم. قال: وقُتل بعضهم على بعض، وما أصيب من الناس يومئذ إلا رجلان. فقال علي رضي الله عنه: التمسوا فيهم المُخْدَج. فالتمسوه، فلم يجدوه. فقام علي رضي الله عنه بنفسه حتى أتى ناسًا قد قُتل بعضهم على بعض، قال: أخّروهم. فوجدوه مما يلي الأرض، فكبر ثم قال: صدق الله، وبلغ رسوله. قال: فقام إليه عبيدة السلماني فقال: يا أمير المؤمنين، آلله الذي لا إله إلا هو، لسمعت هذا الحديث من رسول الله ﷺ؟ فقال: إي والله الذي لا إله إلا هو. حتى استحلفه ثلاثًا، وهو يحلف له.
 صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٠٦٦:١٥٦).
7682 — Zayd ibn Wahb al-Juhani was in the army that was with ‘Ali, may God be pleased with him, which marched against the Kharijites. ‘Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: “People, I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘A people will emerge from my nation who recite the Quran. Your recitation will be nothing compared to their recitation, your prayer will be nothing compared to their prayer, and your fasting will be nothing compared to their fasting. They recite the Quran thinking it is for them, while it is against them. Their prayer will not pass beyond their collarbones. They will pass out of Islam as an arrow passes through the prey.’
 If the army who strikes them knew what had been decreed for them upon the tongue of their Prophet ﷺ, they would rely upon that and abandon work. The sign of that is that among them is a man who has an upper arm but no forearm; at the end of his upper arm is something like the nipple of a breast, with white hairs upon it. Will you go to Mu‘awiyah and the people of Syria and leave these people behind you among your children and wealth? By God, I hope that these are those people, for they have shed inviolable blood and raided the people’s grazing animals. So march in the name of God.”
 Salamah ibn Kuhayl said: Zayd ibn Wahb described the places to me until he said: We passed over a bridge. When we met, the Kharijites that day were led by ‘Abdullah ibn Wahb al-Rasibi. He said to them: “Throw down the spears and draw your swords from their sheaths, for I fear that they will appeal to you as they appealed to you on the day of Harura’.” So they returned, cast aside their spears, and drew their swords. The people thrust at them with spears. He said: They were killed one upon another, and only two of the people were injured that day. ‘Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: “Search among them for the defective one.” They searched but did not find him. Then ‘Ali himself stood up and came to people who had been killed piled upon one another. He said: “Move them back.” They found him beneath them, so he proclaimed greatness and said: “God spoke the truth, and His Messenger conveyed.” Then ‘Ubaydah al-Salmani stood and said: “Commander of the believers, by God, besides whom there is no deity, did you truly hear this hadith from the Messenger of God ﷺ?” He said: “Yes, by God, besides whom there is no deity.” He made him swear three times, and he swore to him.
 Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1066:156).

٧٦٨٣ — عن محمد بن جبير بن مطعم أنه كان يحدث: أنه بلغ معاوية، وهو عنده في وفد من قريش، أن عبد الله بن عمرو يحدث أنه سيكون ملك من قحطان، فغضب، فقام فأثنى على الله بما هو أهله، ثم قال: أما بعد، فإنه بلغني أن رجالًا منكم يحدثون أحاديث ليست في كتاب الله، ولا تؤثر عن رسول الله ﷺ، وأولئك جهالكم، فإياكم والأماني التي تضل أهلها، فإني سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول: ((إن هذا الأمر في قريش، لا يعاديهم أحد إلا كبه الله في النار على وجهه، ما أقاموا الدين)).
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٧١٣٩).
لا خلاف بين أهل العلم من أهل السنة والجماعة أن الإمام الأعظم — أقصد به الحاكم على جميع الأمصار الإسلامية — يُشترط أن يكون قرشيًا، ولكن النصوص الشرعية دلت على أن ذلك التقديم الواجب لهم في الإمامة مشروط بإقامتهم الدين، وإطاعتهم لله ورسوله. فإن خالفوا أمر الله، فتقديم غيرهم ممن يطيع الله تعالى، وينفذ أوامره، ويقيم حدوده أولى منه.
 والشاهد على ذلك قوله ﷺ: ((ما أقاموا الدين))؛ لأن لفظة “ما” مصدرية ظرفية، مقيدة لقوله: ((إن هذا الأمر في قريش)). وتقرير المعنى: إن هذا الأمر يكون في قريش مدة إقامتهم الدين. ومفهومه: أنهم إن لم يقيموا الدين لم يكن فيهم.

7683 — Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut‘im narrated that it reached Mu‘awiyah, while he was with him in a delegation from Quraysh, that ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr was narrating that there would be a king from Qahtan. So he became angry, stood up, praised God as He deserves, then said: “As for what follows: It has reached me that some men among you narrate reports that are not in the Book of God and are not transmitted from the Messenger of God ﷺ. Those are your ignorant ones. Beware of hopes that mislead their people, for I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: ‘This affair is among Quraysh. No one opposes them except that God will throw him into the Fire upon his face, so long as they establish the religion.’”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (7139).
There is no disagreement among the scholars of the people of the Prophetic way and the Muslim community that the supreme leader — meaning the ruler over all Islamic lands — is required to be from Quraysh. However, the legal texts indicate that this required preference for them in leadership is conditional upon their establishing the religion and obeying God and His Messenger. If they oppose the command of God, then giving precedence to others who obey God the Exalted, implement His commands, and establish His prescribed limits is more appropriate.
 The proof for this is his statement ﷺ: “so long as they establish the religion,” because the expression “so long as” is a time-related qualifier attached to his statement: “This affair is among Quraysh.” The meaning is: this affair remains in Quraysh for the duration that they establish the religion. Its implication is that if they do not establish the religion, then it is not for them.

٧٦٨٤ — عن معاوية قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((الناس تبع لقريش في هذا الأمر، خيارهم في الجاهلية خيارهم في الإسلام إذا فقهوا، والله لولا أن تبطر قريش لأخبرتها ما لخيارها عند الله عز وجل)).
 صحيح: رواه أحمد (١٦٩٢٧)، وابن أبي شيبة (٣٣٠٥٤).

7684 — Mu‘awiyah said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “People follow Quraysh in this affair. The best of them in the age of ignorance are the best of them in Islam when they gain understanding. By God, were it not that Quraysh might become arrogant, I would have informed them of what their best have with God, Mighty and Majestic.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Ahmad (16927) and Ibn Abi Shaybah (33054).

7686 — Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “I have a right over Quraysh, and Quraysh has a right over you, so long as when they rule, they act justly; when they are entrusted, they fulfill the trust; and when mercy is sought from them, they show mercy. Whoever does not do that, upon him is the curse of God.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Ahmad (7653) from ‘Abd al-Razzaq — and it is in his Musannaf (19902), with this wording — and graded authentic by Ibn Hibban (4581).

٧٦٨٩ — عن جابر بن سمرة قال: سمعت النبي ﷺ يقول: ((لا يزال أمر الناس ماضيًا ما وليهم اثنا عشر رجلًا)). ثم تكلم النبي ﷺ بكلمة خفيت علي، فسألت أبي: ماذا قال رسول الله ﷺ؟ فقال: ((كلهم من قريش)).
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٧٢٢٢، ٧٢٢٣)، ومسلم (١٨٢١:٦)، والسياق لمسلم. ورواه مسلم من طريق آخر بلفظ: ((لا يزال هذا الدين عزيزًا منيعًا إلى اثني عشر خليفة)).

7689 — Jabir ibn Samurah said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “The affair of the people will continue to proceed as long as twelve men rule them.” Then the Prophet ﷺ said a word that was unclear to me, so I asked my father: “What did the Messenger of God ﷺ say?” He said: “All of them are from Quraysh.”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (7222, 7223) and Muslim (1821:6). The wording is from Muslim. Muslim also narrated it through another route with the wording: “This religion will remain mighty and protected until there have been twelve caliphs.”

٧٦٩٠ — عن عامر بن سعد بن أبي وقاص قال: كتبت إلى جابر بن سمرة مع غلامي نافع: أخبرني بشيء سمعته من رسول الله ﷺ. قال: فكتب إليَّ: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يوم جمعة، عشية رُجم الأسلمي، يقول: ((لا يزال الدين قائمًا حتى تقوم الساعة، أو يكون عليكم اثنا عشر خليفة، كلهم من قريش)).
 وسمعته يقول: ((عُصَيْبَةٌ من المسلمين يفتتحون البيت الأبيض، بيت كسرى أو آل كسرى)).
 وسمعته يقول: ((إن بين يدي الساعة كذابين فاحذروهم)).
 وسمعته يقول: ((إذا أعطى الله أحدكم خيرًا فليبدأ بنفسه وأهل بيته)).
 وسمعته يقول: ((أنا الفرط على الحوض)).
 صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٨٢٢:١٠).

7690 — ‘Amir ibn Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas said: I wrote to Jabir ibn Samurah through my servant Nafi‘, saying: “Inform me of something you heard from the Messenger of God ﷺ.” He wrote back to me: “I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ on a Friday, on the evening when the Aslami man was stoned, saying: ‘The religion will remain established until the Hour comes, or until there have been over you twelve caliphs, all of them from Quraysh.’
 I also heard him say: ‘A small group of Muslims will conquer the White House, the house of Chosroes or the family of Chosroes.’
 I heard him say: ‘Before the Hour there will be liars, so beware of them.’
 I heard him say: ‘When God gives one of you good, let him begin with himself and his household.’
 And I heard him say: ‘I will be the one who reaches the Basin before you.’”
 Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1822:10).

٧٦٩١ — عن النعمان بن بشير قال: كنا قعودًا في المسجد مع رسول الله ﷺ، وكان بشير رجلًا يكف حديثه، فجاء أبو ثعلبة الخشني فقال: يا بشير بن سعد، أتحفظ حديث رسول الله ﷺ في الأمراء؟ فقال حذيفة: أنا أحفظ خطبته. فجلس أبو ثعلبة، فقال حذيفة: قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((تكون النبوة فيكم ما شاء الله أن تكون، ثم يرفعها إذا شاء أن يرفعها، ثم تكون خلافة على منهاج النبوة، فتكون ما شاء الله أن تكون، ثم يرفعها إذا شاء الله أن يرفعها، ثم تكون ملكًا عاضًّا، فيكون ما شاء الله أن يكون، ثم يرفعها إذا شاء أن يرفعها، ثم تكون ملكًا جبرية، فتكون ما شاء الله أن تكون، ثم يرفعها إذا شاء أن يرفعها، ثم تكون خلافة على منهاج النبوة)) ثم سكت.
 قال حبيب: فلما قام عمر بن عبد العزيز، وكان يزيد بن النعمان بن بشير في صحابته، فكتبت إليه بهذا الحديث أذكره إياه، فقلت له: إني أرجو أن يكون أمير المؤمنين — يعني عمر — بعد الملك العاض والجبرية. فأُدخل كتابي على عمر بن عبد العزيز، فسرَّ به وأعجبه.
 حسن: رواه أحمد (١٨٤٠٦).

english_source:
7691 — Al-Nu‘man ibn Bashir said: We were sitting in the mosque with the Messenger of God ﷺ, and Bashir was a man who spoke little. Abu Tha‘labah al-Khushani came and said: “Bashir ibn Sa‘d, do you remember the hadith of the Messenger of God ﷺ concerning rulers?” Hudhayfah said: “I remember his sermon.” So Abu Tha‘labah sat down, and Hudhayfah said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “Prophethood will remain among you for as long as God wills it to remain, then He will raise it when He wills to raise it. Then there will be caliphate upon the method of prophethood, and it will remain for as long as God wills it to remain, then He will raise it when God wills to raise it. Then there will be biting kingship, and it will remain for as long as God wills it to remain, then He will raise it when He wills to raise it. Then there will be coercive kingship, and it will remain for as long as God wills it to remain, then He will raise it when He wills to raise it. Then there will be caliphate upon the method of prophethood.” Then he became silent.
 Habib said: When ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz became ruler, and Yazid ibn al-Nu‘man ibn Bashir was among his companions, I wrote this hadith to him to remind him of it. I said to him: “I hope that the Commander of the Believers — meaning ‘Umar — is after the biting and coercive kingship.” My letter was brought to ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz, and he was pleased with it and admired it.
 Good: Narrated by Ahmad (18406).

٧٦٩٢ — عن أبي برزة يرفعه إلى النبي ﷺ قال: ((الأئمة من قريش، إذا استُرحموا رحموا، وإذا عاهدوا وفوا، وإذا حكموا عدلوا، فمن لم يفعل ذلك منهم فعليه لعنة الله والملائكة والناس أجمعين)).
 حسن: رواه أحمد (١٩٧٧٧).

7692 — Abu Barzah traced it back to the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “The leaders are from Quraysh. When mercy is sought from them, they show mercy; when they make a covenant, they fulfill it; and when they judge, they judge justly. Whoever among them does not do that, upon him is the curse of God, the angels, and all people.”
 Good: Narrated by Ahmad (19777).

٧٦٩٣ — عن الحارث بن أبي الحارث، وكثير بن مرة، وعمرو بن الأسود، وأبي أمامة، عن النبي ﷺ قال: ((إن خيار أئمة قريش خيار أئمة الناس)).
 حسن: رواه الطبراني في الكبير (٨/١٢٨)، والبخاري في التاريخ الكبير (٢/٢٦٢).

 Good: Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Kabir (8/128) and al-Bukhari in al-Tarikh al-Kabir (2/262).

7694 — Anas said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The rulers are from Quraysh so long as they act among you according to three things: they show mercy when mercy is sought from them, they are fair when they distribute, and they are just when they judge.”
 Good: Narrated by al-Hakim (4/501) and al-Bayhaqi (8/144).

٧٦٩٥ — عن سعيد بن جُمهان، عن سفينة قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((خلافة النبوة ثلاثون سنة، ثم يؤتي الله الملك — أو ملكه — من يشاء)).
 قال سعيد: قال لي سفينة: أمسك عليك أبا بكر سنتين، وعمر عشرًا، وعثمان اثنتي عشرة، وعلي كذا.
 قال سعيد: قلت لسفينة: إن هؤلاء يزعمون أن عليًا لم يكن بخليفة. قال: كذبت أستاه بني الزرقاء — يعني بني مروان. هذا لفظ أبي داود.
 ولفظ أحمد: قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((الخلافة ثلاثون عامًا، ثم يكون بعد ذلك الملك)).
 قال سفينة: أمسك خلافة أبي بكر سنتين، وخلافة عمر عشر سنين، وخلافة عثمان اثنتي عشرة سنة، وخلافة علي ست سنين.

7695 — Sa‘id ibn Jumhan narrated from Safinah that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The Prophetic caliphate will last thirty years, then God will give kingship — or His kingship — to whom He wills.”
 Sa‘id said: Safinah said to me: “Count Abu Bakr as two years, ‘Umar as ten, ‘Uthman as twelve, and ‘Ali as such-and-such.”
 Sa‘id said: I said to Safinah: “These people claim that ‘Ali was not a caliph.” He said: “The backsides of the sons of al-Zarqa’ have lied,” meaning the sons of Marwan. This is the wording of Abu Dawud.
 The wording of Ahmad is: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “The caliphate will be thirty years, then after that there will be kingship.”
 Safinah said: “Count the caliphate of Abu Bakr as two years, the caliphate of ‘Umar as ten years, the caliphate of ‘Uthman as twelve years, and the caliphate of ‘Ali as six years.”
 Good: Narrated by Abu Dawud (4646, 4647), al-Tirmidhi (2226), who graded it good, Ahmad (21919, 21923, 21928), Ibn Hibban (6943), who authenticated it, and al-Hakim (3/71, 145).

٧٦٩٦ — عن عبد الله بن عمر قال: قيل لعمر: ألا تستخلف؟ قال: إن أستخلف فقد استخلف من هو خير مني: أبو بكر، وإن أترك فقد ترك من هو خير مني: رسول الله ﷺ. فأثنوا عليه، فقال: راغب راهب، وددت أني نجوت منها كفافًا، لا لي ولا علي، لا أتحملها حيًا ولا ميتًا.
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٧٢١٨)، ومسلم (١٨٢٣:١١).

7696 — ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar said: It was said to ‘Umar: “Will you not appoint a successor?” He said: “If I appoint a successor, then one better than me appointed a successor: Abu Bakr. And if I leave it, then one better than me left it: the Messenger of God ﷺ.” They praised him, and he said: “One hoping and fearing. I wish that I could escape it evenly, neither for me nor against me. I do not want to bear it alive or dead.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (7218) and Muslim (1823:11).

٧٦٩٧ — عن ابن عمر قال: دخلت على حفصة، فقالت: أعلمت أن أباك غير مستخلف؟ قال: قلت: ما كان ليفعل. قالت: إنه فاعل. قال: فحلفت أني أكلمه في ذلك، فسكت، حتى غدوت ولم أكلمه. قال: فكنت كأنما أحمل بيميني جبلًا حتى رجعت، فدخلت عليه، فسألني عن حال الناس، وأنا أخبره. قال: ثم قلت له: إني سمعت الناس يقولون مقالة، فآليت أن أقولها لك: زعموا أنك غير مستخلف، وإنه لو كان لك راعي إبل أو راعي غنم، ثم جاءك وتركها، رأيت أن قد ضيع، فرعاية الناس أشد. قال: فوافقه قولي، فوضع رأسه ساعة، ثم رفعه إلي فقال: إن الله عز وجل يحفظ دينه، وإني لئن لا أستخلف، فإن رسول الله ﷺ لم يستخلف، وإن أستخلف، فإن أبا بكر قد استخلف. قال: فوالله، ما هو إلا أن ذكر رسول الله ﷺ وأبا بكر، فعلمت أنه لم يكن ليعدل برسول الله ﷺ أحدًا، وأنه غير مستخلف.
 صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٨٢٣:١٢).

7697 — Ibn ‘Umar said: I entered upon Hafsah, and she said: “Do you know that your father is not appointing a successor?” I said: “He would not do that.” She said: “He will.” So I swore that I would speak to him about it, but I remained silent until morning and did not speak to him. He said: It was as though I was carrying a mountain because of my oath until I returned and entered upon him. He asked me about the condition of the people, and I informed him. Then I said to him: “I heard the people saying something, and I swore that I would say it to you. They claim that you are not appointing a successor. If you had a shepherd of camels or a shepherd of sheep, then he came to you after leaving them, you would think he had neglected them. Caring for the people is even more serious.” He said: My statement agreed with him, so he lowered his head for a while, then raised it toward me and said: “God, Mighty and Majestic, will preserve His religion. If I do not appoint a successor, then the Messenger of God ﷺ did not appoint one. And if I appoint a successor, then Abu Bakr appointed one.” He said: By God, as soon as he mentioned the Messenger of God ﷺ and Abu Bakr, I knew that he would not equate anyone with the Messenger of God ﷺ, and that he would not appoint a successor.
 Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1823:12).

٧٦٩٧ — عن ابن عمر قال: دخلت على حفصة، فقالت: أعلمت أن أباك غير مستخلف؟ قال: قلت: ما كان ليفعل. قالت: إنه فاعل. قال: فحلفت أني أكلمه في ذلك، فسكت، حتى غدوت ولم أكلمه. قال: فكنت كأنما أحمل بيميني جبلًا حتى رجعت، فدخلت عليه، فسألني عن حال الناس، وأنا أخبره. قال: ثم قلت له: إني سمعت الناس يقولون مقالة، فآليت أن أقولها لك: زعموا أنك غير مستخلف، وإنه لو كان لك راعي إبل أو راعي غنم، ثم جاءك وتركها، رأيت أن قد ضيع، فرعاية الناس أشد. قال: فوافقه قولي، فوضع رأسه ساعة، ثم رفعه إلي فقال: إن الله عز وجل يحفظ دينه، وإني لئن لا أستخلف، فإن رسول الله ﷺ لم يستخلف، وإن أستخلف، فإن أبا بكر قد استخلف. قال: فوالله، ما هو إلا أن ذكر رسول الله ﷺ وأبا بكر، فعلمت أنه لم يكن ليعدل برسول الله ﷺ أحدًا، وأنه غير مستخلف.
 صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٨٢٣:١٢).
7697 — Ibn ‘Umar said: I entered upon Hafsah, and she said: “Do you know that your father is not appointing a successor?” I said: “He would not do that.” She said: “He will.” So I swore that I would speak to him about it, but I remained silent until morning and did not speak to him. He said: It was as though I was carrying a mountain because of my oath until I returned and entered upon him. He asked me about the condition of the people, and I informed him. Then I said to him: “I heard the people saying something, and I swore that I would say it to you. They claim that you are not appointing a successor. If you had a shepherd of camels or a shepherd of sheep, then he came to you after leaving them, you would think he had neglected them. Caring for the people is even more serious.” He said: My statement agreed with him, so he lowered his head for a while, then raised it toward me and said: “God, Mighty and Majestic, will preserve His religion. If I do not appoint a successor, then the Messenger of God ﷺ did not appoint one. And if I appoint a successor, then Abu Bakr appointed one.” He said: By God, as soon as he mentioned the Messenger of God ﷺ and Abu Bakr, I knew that he would not equate anyone with the Messenger of God ﷺ, and that he would not appoint a successor.
 Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1823:12).

٧٦٩٨ — عن عمرو بن ميمون الأودي قال: رأيت عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه قال: يا عبد الله بن عمر، اذهب إلى أم المؤمنين عائشة رضي الله عنها فقل: يقرأ عمر بن الخطاب عليك السلام، ثم سلها أن أدفن مع صاحبيَّ. قالت: كنت أريده لنفسي، فلأوثرنه اليوم على نفسي. فلما أقبل قال له: ما لديك؟ قال: أذنت لك يا أمير المؤمنين. قال: ما كان شيء أهم إلي من ذلك المضجع، فإذا قُبِضت فاحملوني، ثم سلّموا، ثم قل: يستأذن عمر بن الخطاب، فإن أذنت لي فادفنوني، وإلا فردوني إلى مقابر المسلمين. إني لا أعلم أحدًا أحق بهذا الأمر من هؤلاء النفر الذين توفي رسول الله ﷺ وهو عنهم راض، فمن استخلفوا بعدي فهو الخليفة، فاسمعوا له وأطيعوا. فسمى عثمان، وعليًا، وطلحة، والزبير، وعبد الرحمن بن عوف، وسعد بن أبي وقاص. وولج عليه شاب من الأنصار فقال: أبشر يا أمير المؤمنين ببشرى الله، كان لك من القدم في الإسلام ما قد علمت، ثم استخلفت فعدلت، ثم الشهادة بعد هذا كله. فقال: ليتني يا ابن أخي، وذلك كفافًا لا علي ولا لي. أوصي الخليفة من بعدي بالمهاجرين الأولين خيرًا، أن يعرف لهم حقهم، وأن يحفظ لهم حرمتهم. وأوصيه بالأنصار خيرًا، الذين تبوؤوا الدار والإيمان، أن يقبل من محسنهم، ويعفى عن مسيئهم. وأوصيه بذمة الله وذمة رسوله ﷺ، أن يوفى لهم بعهدهم، وأن يقاتل من ورائهم، وأن لا يكلفوا فوق طاقتهم.
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (١٣٩٢).

7698 — ‘Amr ibn Maymun al-Awdi said: I saw ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, say: “‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar, go to the Mother of the Believers ‘A’ishah, may God be pleased with her, and say: ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab sends you greetings of peace. Then ask her that I be buried with my two companions.” She said: “I had wanted it for myself, but today I will prefer him over myself.” When he returned, ‘Umar said to him: “What do you have?” He said: “She has granted permission for you, Commander of the Believers.” He said: “Nothing was more important to me than that resting place. When I am taken in death, carry me, then give greetings of peace, then say: ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab seeks permission. If she gives permission, bury me there; otherwise return me to the graveyard of the Muslims. I do not know anyone more entitled to this affair than these individuals with whom the Messenger of God ﷺ was pleased when he died. Whoever they appoint after me is the caliph, so listen to him and obey.” He named ‘Uthman, ‘Ali, Talhah, al-Zubayr, ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf, and Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas. A young man from the Ansar entered upon him and said: “Receive glad tidings, Commander of the Believers, with the glad tidings of God. You had precedence in Islam as you know, then you were appointed and acted justly, then martyrdom after all of this.” He said: “I wish, my nephew, that it would be just even: neither against me nor for me. I advise the caliph after me to treat the early Emigrants well, to recognize their rights and preserve their honor. I advise him to treat the Helpers well, those who settled the city and faith, to accept from those among them who do good and pardon those who do wrong. And I advise him concerning the covenant of God and the covenant of His Messenger ﷺ, that their agreement be fulfilled, that they be defended from behind, and that they not be burdened beyond their ability.”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (1392).

٧٦٩٩ — عن المسور بن مخرمة: أن الرهط الذين ولّاهم عمر اجتمعوا فتشاوروا، فقال لهم عبد الرحمن: لست بالذي أنافسكم على هذا الأمر، ولكنكم إن شئتم اخترت لكم منكم. فجعلوا ذلك إلى عبد الرحمن. فلما ولوا عبد الرحمن أمرهم، مال الناس على عبد الرحمن، حتى ما أرى أحدًا من الناس يتبع أولئك الرهط، ولا يطأ عقبه، ومال الناس على عبد الرحمن يشاورونه تلك الليالي، حتى إذا كانت الليلة التي أصبحنا منها، فبايعنا عثمان.
 قال المسور: طرقني عبد الرحمن بعد هجع من الليل، فضرب الباب حتى استيقظت، فقال: أراك نائمًا، فوالله ما اكتحلت هذه الليلة بكبير نوم، انطلق فادع الزبير وسعدًا. فدعوتهما له، فشاورهما، ثم دعاني فقال: ادع لي عليًا. فدعوته، فناجاه حتى ابهار الليل، ثم قام علي من عنده وهو على طمع، وقد كان عبد الرحمن يخشى من علي شيئًا، ثم قال: ادع لي عثمان. فدعوته، فناجاه حتى فرّق بينهما المؤذن بالصبح. فلما صلى للناس الصبح، واجتمع أولئك الرهط عند المنبر، أرسل إلى من كان حاضرًا من المهاجرين والأنصار، وأرسل إلى أمراء الأجناد، وكانوا وافوا تلك الحجة مع عمر. فلما اجتمعوا، تشهد عبد الرحمن، ثم قال: أما بعد، يا علي، إني قد نظرت في أمر الناس، فلم أرهم يعدلون بعثمان، فلا تجعلَنَّ على نفسك سبيلًا. فقال: أبايعك على سنة الله ورسوله، والخليفتين من بعده. فبايعه عبد الرحمن، وبايعه الناس: المهاجرون والأنصار، وأمراء الأجناد، والمسلمون.
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٧٢٠٧).

 قال المسور: طرقني عبد الرحمن بعد هجع من الليل، فضرب الباب حتى استيقظت، فقال: أراك نائمًا، فوالله ما اكتحلت هذه الليلة بكبير نوم، انطلق فادع الزبير وسعدًا. فدعوتهما له، فشاورهما، ثم دعاني فقال: ادع لي عليًا. فدعوته، فناجاه حتى ابهار الليل، ثم قام علي من عنده وهو على طمع، وقد كان عبد الرحمن يخشى من علي شيئًا، ثم قال: ادع لي عثمان. فدعوته، فناجاه حتى فرّق بينهما المؤذن بالصبح. فلما صلى للناس الصبح، واجتمع أولئك الرهط عند المنبر، أرسل إلى من كان حاضرًا من المهاجرين والأنصار، وأرسل إلى أمراء الأجناد، وكانوا وافوا تلك الحجة مع عمر. فلما اجتمعوا، تشهد عبد الرحمن، ثم قال: أما بعد، يا علي، إني قد نظرت في أمر الناس، فلم أرهم يعدلون بعثمان، فلا تجعلَنَّ على نفسك سبيلًا. فقال: أبايعك على سنة الله ورسوله، والخليفتين من بعده. فبايعه عبد الرحمن، وبايعه الناس: المهاجرون والأنصار، وأمراء الأجناد، والمسلمون.

7699 — Al-Miswar ibn Makhramah narrated that the group whom ‘Umar appointed gathered and consulted. ‘Abd al-Rahman said to them: “I will not compete with you for this matter, but if you wish, I will choose one from among you for you.” So they entrusted that to ‘Abd al-Rahman. When they entrusted their matter to ‘Abd al-Rahman, the people turned to ‘Abd al-Rahman, until I did not see anyone among the people following that group or walking behind them. The people turned to ‘Abd al-Rahman, consulting him during those nights, until the night after which we woke and pledged allegiance to ‘Uthman.
 Al-Miswar said: ‘Abd al-Rahman came to me after a portion of the night had passed and knocked on the door until I woke up. He said: “I see that you are sleeping. By God, I have not had much sleep this night. Go and call al-Zubayr and Sa‘d.” So I called them for him, and he consulted them. Then he called me and said: “Call ‘Ali for me.” So I called him, and he spoke privately with him until the night became very dark. Then ‘Ali left him while still hoping for the matter, and ‘Abd al-Rahman had feared something from ‘Ali. Then he said: “Call ‘Uthman for me.” So I called him, and he spoke privately with him until the caller to prayer separated them at dawn. When he led the people in the dawn prayer and that group gathered near the pulpit, he sent for those present from the Emigrants and the Helpers, and he sent for the commanders of the armies, who had attended that pilgrimage with ‘Umar. When they gathered, ‘Abd al-Rahman testified, then said: “As for what follows: ‘Ali, I have looked into the matter of the people, and I do not see them equating anyone with ‘Uthman, so do not make a case against yourself.” He said: “I pledge allegiance to you upon the way of God and His Messenger, and the two caliphs after him.” So ‘Abd al-Rahman pledged allegiance to him, and the people pledged allegiance to him: the Emigrants, the Helpers, the commanders of the armies, and the Muslims.
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (7207).

٧٧٠٠ — عن عمرو بن ميمون قال: فلما قُبض — يعني عمر بن الخطاب — خرجنا به، فانطلقنا نمشي، فسلم عبد الله بن عمر، قال: يستأذن عمر بن الخطاب. قالت: أدخلوه. فأُدخل، فوضع هنالك مع صاحبيه. فلما فُرغ من دفنه اجتمع هؤلاء الرهط، فقال عبد الرحمن: اجعلوا أمركم إلى ثلاثة منكم. فقال الزبير: قد جعلت أمري إلى علي. وقال طلحة: قد جعلت أمري إلى عثمان. وقال سعد: قد جعلت أمري إلى عبد الرحمن بن عوف. فقال عبد الرحمن: أيكما تبرأ من هذا الأمر، فنجعله إليه، والله عليه والإسلام، لينظرن أفضلهم في نفسه؟ فأسكت الشيخان. فقال عبد الرحمن: أفتجعلونه إليَّ، والله عليَّ أن لا آلو عن أفضلكم؟ قالا: نعم. فأخذ بيد أحدهما، فقال: لك قرابة من رسول الله ﷺ، والقدم في الإسلام ما قد علمت، فالله عليك لئن أمرتك لتعدلن، ولئن أمرت عثمان، لتسمعن ولتطيعن. ثم خلا بالآخر، فقال له مثل ذلك. فلما أخذ الميثاق قال: ارفع يدك يا عثمان. فبايعه، فبايع له علي، وولج أهل الدار فبايعوه.
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٧٠٠).

7700 — ‘Amr ibn Maymun said: When he was taken in death — meaning ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab — we went out with him and walked. ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar gave greetings of peace and said: “‘Umar ibn al-Khattab seeks permission.” She said: “Bring him in.” So he was brought in and placed there with his two companions. When his burial was completed, those members of the group gathered. ‘Abd al-Rahman said: “Entrust your matter to three among you.” Al-Zubayr said: “I have entrusted my matter to ‘Ali.” Talhah said: “I have entrusted my matter to ‘Uthman.” Sa‘d said: “I have entrusted my matter to ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf.” ‘Abd al-Rahman said: “Which of you two will withdraw from this matter so that we may entrust it to him, with God and Islam upon him, that he will surely look to the one he considers best?” The two elders remained silent. ‘Abd al-Rahman said: “Will you entrust it to me, with God upon me that I will not fall short in choosing the best of you?” They said: “Yes.” He took the hand of one of them and said: “You have kinship with the Messenger of God ﷺ and precedence in Islam as you know. By God, if I appoint you, you must act justly; and if I appoint ‘Uthman, you must listen and obey.” Then he met privately with the other and said the same to him. When he had taken the covenant, he said: “Raise your hand, ‘Uthman.” He pledged allegiance to him, ‘Ali pledged allegiance to him, and the people of the house entered and pledged allegiance to him.
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3700).

By God, if I appoint you, you must act justly; and if I appoint ‘Uthman, you must listen and obey.” Then he met privately with the other and said the same to him. When he had taken the covenant, he said: “Raise your hand, ‘Uthman.” He pledged allegiance to him, ‘Ali pledged allegiance to him, and the people of the house entered and pledged allegiance to him.

٧٧٠٠ — عن عمرو بن ميمون قال: فلما قُبض — يعني عمر بن الخطاب — خرجنا به، فانطلقنا نمشي، فسلم عبد الله بن عمر، قال: يستأذن عمر بن الخطاب. قالت: أدخلوه. فأُدخل، فوضع هنالك مع صاحبيه. فلما فُرغ من دفنه اجتمع هؤلاء الرهط، فقال عبد الرحمن: اجعلوا أمركم إلى ثلاثة منكم. فقال الزبير: قد جعلت أمري إلى علي. وقال طلحة: قد جعلت أمري إلى عثمان. وقال سعد: قد جعلت أمري إلى عبد الرحمن بن عوف. فقال عبد الرحمن: أيكما تبرأ من هذا الأمر، فنجعله إليه، والله عليه والإسلام، لينظرن أفضلهم في نفسه؟ فأسكت الشيخان. فقال عبد الرحمن: أفتجعلونه إليَّ، والله عليَّ أن لا آلو عن أفضلكم؟ قالا: نعم. فأخذ بيد أحدهما، فقال: لك قرابة من رسول الله ﷺ، والقدم في الإسلام ما قد علمت، فالله عليك لئن أمرتك لتعدلن، ولئن أمرت عثمان، لتسمعن ولتطيعن. ثم خلا بالآخر، فقال له مثل ذلك. فلما أخذ الميثاق قال: ارفع يدك يا عثمان. فبايعه، فبايع له علي، وولج أهل الدار فبايعوه.
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٧٠٠).

٧٧٠١ — عن معدان بن أبي طلحة: أن عمر بن الخطاب خطب يوم الجمعة، فذكر نبي الله ﷺ، وذكر أبا بكر، قال: إني رأيت كأن ديكًا نقرني ثلاث نقرات، وإني لا أراه إلا حضور أجلي، وإن أقوامًا يأمرونني أن أستخلف، وإن الله لم يكن ليضيع دينه، ولا خلافته، ولا الذي بعث به نبيه ﷺ، فإن عجل بي أمر، فالخلافة شورى بين هؤلاء الستة الذين توفي رسول الله ﷺ وهو عنهم راض، وإني قد علمت أن أقوامًا يطعنون في هذا الأمر، أنا ضربتهم بيدي هذه على الإسلام، فإن فعلوا ذلك فأولئك أعداء الله الكفرة الضلال.
 صحيح: رواه مسلم (٥٦٧:٧٨).

7701 — Ma‘dan ibn Abi Talhah narrated that ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab delivered a sermon on Friday, mentioned the Prophet of God ﷺ, and mentioned Abu Bakr. He said: “I saw as though a rooster pecked me three pecks, and I only see that as the coming of my death. Some people are telling me to appoint a successor. God would never let His religion, His caliphate, or that with which He sent His Prophet ﷺ be lost. If a matter comes quickly upon me, then the caliphate is to be decided by consultation among these six men with whom the Messenger of God ﷺ was pleased when he died. I know that some people will criticize this matter, though I struck them with this hand of mine for Islam. If they do that, then they are the enemies of God, disbelieving and misguided.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (567:78).

٧٧٠٢ — عن ابن عباس قال: قدم مسيلمة الكذاب على عهد رسول الله ﷺ، فجعل يقول: إن جعل لي محمد الأمر من بعده تبعته. وقدمها في بشر كثير من قومه. فأقبل إليه رسول الله ﷺ ومعه ثابت بن قيس بن شماس، وفي يد رسول الله ﷺ قطعة جريد، حتى وقف على مسيلمة في أصحابه. فقال: ((لو سألتني هذه القطعة ما أعطيتكها، ولن تعدو أمر الله فيك، ولئن أدبرت ليعقرنك الله، وإني لأراك الذي أُريت فيك ما رأيت، وهذا ثابت يجيبك عني)) ثم انصرف عنه.
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٦٢٠)، ومسلم (٢٢٧٣:٢١).
 قوله: ((إن جعل لي محمد الأمر من بعده)) أي الخلافة.
 وقول النبي ﷺ: ((إني لأراك الذي أُريت فيك)) يشير إلى الرؤيا التي رآها، وهي كما قال عبيد الله بن عبد الله: سألت عبد الله بن عباس عن رؤيا رسول الله ﷺ التي ذكرها، فقال ابن عباس: ذكر لي رسول الله ﷺ قال: ((بينا أنا نائم، أُريت أنه وضع في يدي سواران من ذهب، ففظعتهما وكرهتهما، فأذن لي فنفختهما فطارا، فأولتهما كذابين يخرجان)). فقال عبيد الله: أحدهما العنسي الذي قتله فيروز باليمن، والآخر مسيلمة الكذاب. ذكره البخاري (٤٣٧٩).
 وقوله: “في دار بنت الحارث، وإن تحته ابنة الحارث بن كريز”؛ تحته أي كانت زوجةً لمسيلمة الكذاب قبل أن تتزوج بغيره، ولذلك نزل مسيلمة مع قومه عندها. وكان عددهم سبعة عشر نفرًا، كما ذكره الواقدي.

7702 — Ibn ‘Abbas said: Musaylimah the Liar came during the time of the Messenger of God ﷺ and began saying: “If Muhammad appoints me to the affair after him, I will follow him.” He came with many people from his tribe. The Messenger of God ﷺ approached him, with Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, and in the hand of the Messenger of God ﷺ was a piece of palm stalk, until he stood over Musaylimah among his companions. He said: “If you asked me for this piece, I would not give it to you. You will not go beyond what God has decreed for you. If you turn away, God will destroy you. I see that you are the one concerning whom I was shown what I saw. This is Thabit; he will answer you on my behalf.” Then he turned away from him.
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3620) and Muslim (2273:21).
 His statement, “If Muhammad appoints me to the affair after him,” means the caliphate.
 The Prophet’s statement ﷺ, “I see that you are the one concerning whom I was shown,” refers to the vision he saw. ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah said: I asked ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas about the vision of the Messenger of God ﷺ that he mentioned, and Ibn ‘Abbas said: The Messenger of God ﷺ told me: “While I was sleeping, I was shown that two bracelets of gold had been placed in my hands. I was disturbed by them and disliked them, then I was given permission and blew upon them, so they flew away. I interpreted them as two liars who would emerge.” ‘Ubaydullah said: One of them was al-‘Ansi, whom Fayruz killed in Yemen, and the other was Musaylimah the Liar. Al-Bukhari mentioned it (4379).
 The phrase “in the house of the daughter of al-Harith, and beneath him was the daughter of al-Harith ibn Kurayz” means she was the wife of Musaylimah the Liar before she married another, and for that reason Musaylimah and his people stayed with her. Their number was seventeen men, as al-Waqidi mentioned.

٧٧٠٢ — عن ابن عباس قال: قدم مسيلمة الكذاب على عهد رسول الله ﷺ، فجعل يقول: إن جعل لي محمد الأمر من بعده تبعته. وقدمها في بشر كثير من قومه. فأقبل إليه رسول الله ﷺ ومعه ثابت بن قيس بن شماس، وفي يد رسول الله ﷺ قطعة جريد، حتى وقف على مسيلمة في أصحابه. فقال: ((لو سألتني هذه القطعة ما أعطيتكها، ولن تعدو أمر الله فيك، ولئن أدبرت ليعقرنك الله، وإني لأراك الذي أُريت فيك ما رأيت، وهذا ثابت يجيبك عني)) ثم انصرف عنه.
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣٦٢٠)، ومسلم (٢٢٧٣:٢١).
 قوله: ((إن جعل لي محمد الأمر من بعده)) أي الخلافة.
 وقول النبي ﷺ: ((إني لأراك الذي أُريت فيك)) يشير إلى الرؤيا التي رآها، وهي كما قال عبيد الله بن عبد الله: سألت عبد الله بن عباس عن رؤيا رسول الله ﷺ التي ذكرها، فقال ابن عباس: ذكر لي رسول الله ﷺ قال: ((بينا أنا نائم، أُريت أنه وضع في يدي سواران من ذهب، ففظعتهما وكرهتهما، فأذن لي فنفختهما فطارا، فأولتهما كذابين يخرجان)). فقال عبيد الله: أحدهما العنسي الذي قتله فيروز باليمن، والآخر مسيلمة الكذاب. ذكره البخاري (٤٣٧٩).
 وقوله: “في دار بنت الحارث، وإن تحته ابنة الحارث بن كريز”؛ تحته أي كانت زوجةً لمسيلمة الكذاب قبل أن تتزوج بغيره، ولذلك نزل مسيلمة مع قومه عندها. وكان عددهم سبعة عشر نفرًا، كما ذكره الواقدي.
7702 — Ibn ‘Abbas said: Musaylimah the Liar came during the time of the Messenger of God ﷺ and began saying: “If Muhammad appoints me to the affair after him, I will follow him.” He came with many people from his tribe. The Messenger of God ﷺ approached him, with Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, and in the hand of the Messenger of God ﷺ was a piece of palm stalk, until he stood over Musaylimah among his companions. He said: “If you asked me for this piece, I would not give it to you. You will not go beyond what God has decreed for you. If you turn away, God will destroy you. I see that you are the one concerning whom I was shown what I saw. This is Thabit; he will answer you on my behalf.” Then he turned away from him.
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (3620) and Muslim (2273:21).
 His statement, “If Muhammad appoints me to the affair after him,” means the caliphate.
 The Prophet’s statement ﷺ, “I see that you are the one concerning whom I was shown,” refers to the vision he saw. ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah said: I asked ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas about the vision of the Messenger of God ﷺ that he mentioned, and Ibn ‘Abbas said: The Messenger of God ﷺ told me: “While I was sleeping, I was shown that two bracelets of gold had been placed in my hands. I was disturbed by them and disliked them, then I was given permission and blew upon them, so they flew away. I interpreted them as two liars who would emerge.” ‘Ubaydullah said: One of them was al-‘Ansi, whom Fayruz killed in Yemen, and the other was Musaylimah the Liar. Al-Bukhari mentioned it (4379).
 The phrase “in the house of the daughter of al-Harith, and beneath him was the daughter of al-Harith ibn Kurayz” means she was the wife of Musaylimah the Liar before she married another, and for that reason Musaylimah and his people stayed with her. Their number was seventeen men, as al-Waqidi mentioned.

 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٧١٩٨).

٧٧٠٤ — عن أبي أيوب أنه قال: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول: ((ما بُعث من نبي، ولا كان بعده من خليفة، إلا وله بطانتان: بطانة تأمره بالمعروف وتنهاه عن المنكر، وبطانة لا تألوه خبالًا، فمن وُقي بطانة السوء فقد وُقي)).

7704 — Abu Ayyub said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: “No prophet was sent, and no caliph came after him, except that he had two inner circles: an inner circle that commands him to what is right and forbids him from what is wrong, and an inner circle that spares no effort in corrupting him. Whoever is protected from the evil inner circle has been protected.”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Nasa’i (4203), al-Tahawi in Sharh al-Mushkil (2112), and al-Tabarani in al-Kabir (4/156).

7705 — Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “There is no governor except that he has two inner circles: an inner circle that commands him to what is right and forbids him from what is wrong, and an inner circle that spares no effort in corrupting him. Whoever is protected from its evil has been protected, and he will be according to whichever of the two overcomes him.”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Nasa’i (4201), Ahmad (7239), and graded authentic by Ibn Hibban (6191).

٧٧٠٦ — عن عائشة قالت: قال رسول الله ﷺ: ((إذا أراد الله بالأمير خيرًا جعل له وزير صدق، إن نسي ذكّره، وإن ذكر أعانه، وإذا أراد الله به غير ذلك جعل له وزير سوء، إن نسي لم يذكره، وإن ذكر لم يعنه)).
 صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٢٩٣٢) واللفظ له، والنسائي (٤٢٠٤)، وأحمد (٢٤٤١٤)، وابن حبان (٤٤٩٤)، والبيهقي (١٠/١١١-١١٢). وفي بعض طرقه ضعف يسير يتقوى بمجيئه من طرق أخرى.

7706 — ‘A’ishah said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “When God intends good for a ruler, He gives him a truthful minister: if he forgets, he reminds him, and if he remembers, he helps him. And when God intends otherwise for him, He gives him an evil minister: if he forgets, he does not remind him, and if he remembers, he does not help him.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Abu Dawud (2932), with his wording; al-Nasa’i (4204), Ahmad (24414), Ibn Hibban (4494), and al-Bayhaqi (10/111–112). Some of its routes contain slight weakness, which is strengthened by its transmission through other routes.

٧٧٠٧ — عن عدي بن عميرة الكندي قال: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول: ((من استعملناه منكم على عمل، فكتمنا مخيطًا فما فوقه، كان غلولًا يأتي به يوم القيامة)). قال: فقام إليه رجل أسود من الأنصار، كأني أنظر إليه، فقال: يا رسول الله، اقبل عني عملك. قال: ((وما لك؟)) قال: سمعتك تقول كذا وكذا. قال: ((وأنا أقوله الآن: من استعملناه منكم على عمل، فليجيء بقليله وكثيره، فما أوتي منه أخذ، وما نُهي عنه انتهى)).

٧٧٠٨ — عن عقبة بن مالك قال: بعث النبي ﷺ سريةً، فسلَّحتُ رجلًا منهم سيفًا، فلما رجع قال: لو رأيتَ ما لامنا رسول الله ﷺ! قال: ((أعجزتم إذ بعثتُ رجلًا منكم فلم يمضِ لأمري أن تجعلوا مكانه من يمضي لأمري؟)).
 حسن: رواه أبو داود (٢٦٢٧)، وأحمد (١٧٠٠٧)، وصححه ابن حبان (٤٧٤٠)، والحاكم (٢/١١٤-١١٥).
 وقوله: “سلَّحته” أي أعطيته سلاحًا.

english_source:
7708 — ‘Uqbah ibn Malik said: The Prophet ﷺ sent out a detachment, and I equipped one of its men with a sword. When he returned, he said: “If only you had seen how the Messenger of God ﷺ reproached us!” He said: “Were you unable, when I sent a man from among you and he did not carry out my command, to appoint in his place someone who would carry out my command?”
 Good: Narrated by Abu Dawud (2627), Ahmad (17007), and graded authentic by Ibn Hibban (4740) and al-Hakim (2/114–115).
 His phrase “I equipped him” means: I gave him a weapon.

٧٧٠٩ — عن أبي حميد الساعدي قال: استعمل النبي ﷺ رجلًا من بني أسد يقال له: ابن اللُّتْبِيَّة على الصدقة، فلما قدم قال: هذا لكم، وهذا أُهدي لي. فقام النبي ﷺ على المنبر، قال سفيان أيضًا: فصعد المنبر، فحمد الله وأثنى عليه، ثم قال: ((ما بال العامل نبعثه فيأتي يقول: هذا لك، وهذا لي؟ فهلا جلس في بيت أبيه وأمه، فينظر أيُهدى له أم لا؟ والذي نفسي بيده، لا يأتي بشيء إلا جاء به يوم القيامة يحمله على رقبته، إن كان بعيرًا له رغاء، أو بقرةً لها خوار، أو شاةً تَيْعَر)). ثم رفع يديه حتى رأينا عُفرتي إبطيه: ((ألا هل بلغت؟)) ثلاثًا.
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٧١٧٤)، ومسلم (١٨٣٢:٢٦). والسياق للبخاري.

7709 — Abu Humayd al-Sa‘idi said: The Prophet ﷺ appointed a man from Banu Asad called Ibn al-Lutbiyyah over charity collection. When he came back, he said: “This is for you, and this was given to me as a gift.” So the Prophet ﷺ stood on the pulpit. Sufyan also said: He ascended the pulpit, praised God and extolled Him, then said: “What is the matter with a worker whom we send, then he comes and says: ‘This is for you, and this is for me’? Why did he not sit in the house of his father and mother and see whether he would be given gifts or not? By the One in whose hand is my soul, he will not bring anything except that he will come with it on the Day of Resurrection carrying it on his neck: if it is a camel, it will be grunting; if it is a cow, it will be mooing; and if it is a sheep, it will be bleating.” Then he raised his hands until we saw the whiteness of his armpits and said three times: “Have I conveyed?”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (7174) and Muslim (1832:26). The wording is al-Bukhari’s.

٧٧١٠ — عن عبد الله بن السعدي أنه قدم على عمر في خلافته، فقال له عمر: ألم أُحَدَّث أنك تلي من أعمال الناس أعمالًا، فإذا أُعطيت العمالة كرهتها؟ فقلت: بلى. فقال عمر: فما تريد إلى ذلك؟ قلت: إن لي أفراسًا وأعبدًا، وأنا بخير، وأريد أن تكون عمالتي صدقةً على المسلمين. قال عمر: لا تفعل، فإني كنت أردت الذي أردت، فكان رسول الله ﷺ يعطيني العطاء، فأقول: أعطه أفقر إليه مني، حتى أعطاني مرةً مالًا، فقلت: أعطه أفقر إليه مني، فقال النبي ﷺ: ((خذه فتموَّله، وتصدق به، فما جاءك من هذا المال وأنت غير مشرف ولا سائل فخذه، وإلا فلا تتبعه نفسك)).
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٧١٦٣)، ورواه مسلم (١٠٤٥:١١٢) من طريق آخر، عن ابن الساعدي المالكي أنه قال: استعملني عمر بن الخطاب على الصدقة، فلما فرغت منها، وأديتها إليه، أمر لي بعمالة، فقلت: إنما عملت لله، وأجري على الله. فقال: خذ ما أُعطيت، فإني عملت على عهد رسول الله ﷺ فعمَّلني، فقلت مثل قولك، فقال لي رسول الله ﷺ: ((إذا أُعطيت شيئًا من غير أن تسأل فكل وتصدق)).

٧٧١١ — عن طريف أبي تميمة قال: شهدت صفوان وجندبًا وأصحابه، وهو يوصيهم، فقالوا: هل سمعت من رسول الله ﷺ شيئًا؟ قال: سمعته يقول: ((من سمَّع سمَّع الله به يوم القيامة)). قال: ((ومن يشاقق يشقق الله عليه يوم القيامة)). فقالوا: أوصنا. فقال: ((إن أول ما ينتن من الإنسان بطنه، فمن استطاع أن لا يأكل إلا طيبًا فليفعل، ومن استطاع أن لا يُحال بينه وبين الجنة بملء كفه من دم أهراقه فليفعل)).
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٧١٥٢).
 وقوله: “من يشاقق يشقق الله عليه” يحتمل أن تكون من المشقة والإضرار بحمل الناس على ما يشق عليهم من قِبل ولاة أمورهم، ويحتمل أن تكون من الشقاق، وهو الخلاف ومفارقة الجماعة.

english_source:
7711 — Tarif Abu Tamimah said: I was present with Safwan, Jundab, and his companions while he was advising them. They said: “Did you hear anything from the Messenger of God ﷺ?” He said: I heard him say: “Whoever acts so that people hear of him, God will make him heard of on the Day of Resurrection.” He said: “Whoever makes things difficult, God will make things difficult for him on the Day of Resurrection.” They said: “Advise us.” He said: “The first thing of a person to decay is his belly, so whoever is able not to eat except what is pure, let him do so. And whoever is able not to have between himself and Paradise even a handful of blood that he has shed, let him do so.”
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (7152).
 The phrase “Whoever makes things difficult, God will make things difficult for him” may refer to hardship and harm by rulers burdening people with what is difficult for them. It may also refer to dissension, meaning opposition and separating from the community.

 صحيح: رواه مسلم (٢١٢٨:١٢٥).

7713 — Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: “There are two types of the people of the Fire whom I have not seen: people with whips like the tails of cattle with which they beat the people; and women who are clothed yet naked, inclining and causing others to incline, their heads like the leaning humps of Bactrian camels. They will not enter Paradise, nor will they smell its fragrance, even though its fragrance can be found from such-and-such a distance.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2128:125).

They will not enter Paradise, nor will they smell its fragrance, even though its fragrance can be found from such-and-such a distance.”
 Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (2128:125).

٧٧١٦ — عن عبد الله بن عمر قال: بعث رسول الله ﷺ بعثًا، وأمَّر عليهم أسامة بن زيد، فطعن الناس في إمرته، فقام رسول الله ﷺ فقال: ((إن تطعنوا في إمرته، فقد كنتم تطعنون في إمرة أبيه من قبل، وأيم الله إن كان لخليقًا للإمرة، وإن كان لمن أحب الناس إليَّ، وإن هذا لمن أحب الناس إليَّ بعده)).
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٧١٨٧)، ومسلم (٢٤٢٦:٦٣).

7716 — ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar said: The Messenger of God ﷺ sent out an army and appointed Usamah ibn Zayd as its commander. The people criticized his command, so the Messenger of God ﷺ stood and said: “If you criticize his command, you used to criticize the command of his father before. By God, he was certainly worthy of command, and he was among the most beloved of people to me, and this one is among the most beloved of people to me after him.”
 Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhari (7187) and Muslim (2426:63).

٧٧١٧ — عن ابن عمر قال: كان سالم مولى أبي حذيفة يؤم المهاجرين الأولين وأصحاب النبي ﷺ في مسجد قباء، فيهم أبو بكر، وعمر، وأبو سلمة، وزيد، وعامر بن ربيعة.
 وفي رواية: لما قدم المهاجرون الأولون العصبة — موضع بقباء — قبل مقدم رسول الله ﷺ، كان يؤمهم سالم مولى أبي حذيفة، وكان أكثرهم قرآنًا.
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٧١٧٥)، والرواية الأخرى (٦٩٢).

7717 — Ibn ‘Umar said: Salim, the freedman of Abu Hudhayfah, used to lead the first Emigrants and the companions of the Prophet ﷺ in prayer in the Mosque of Quba’. Among them were Abu Bakr, ‘Umar, Abu Salamah, Zayd, and ‘Amir ibn Rabi‘ah.
 In another narration: When the first Emigrants arrived at al-‘Usbah — a place in Quba’ — before the arrival of the Messenger of God ﷺ, Salim, the freedman of Abu Hudhayfah, used to lead them in prayer, and he knew the most Qur’an among them.
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (7175), and the other narration is also by al-Bukhari (692).

٧٧١٨ — عن عامر بن واثلة: أن نافع بن عبد الحارث لقي عمر بعسفان، وكان عمر يستعمله على مكة، فقال: من استعملت على أهل الوادي؟ فقال: ابن أبزى. قال: ومن ابن أبزى؟ قال: مولى من موالينا. قال: فاستخلفت عليهم مولى؟! قال: إنه قارئ لكتاب الله عز وجل، وإنه عالم بالفرائض. قال عمر: أما إن نبيكم ﷺ قد قال: ((إن الله يرفع بهذا الكتاب أقوامًا ويضع به آخرين)).
 صحيح: رواه مسلم (٨١٧:٢٦٩).

7718 — ‘Amir ibn Wathilah narrated that Nafi‘ ibn ‘Abd al-Harith met ‘Umar at ‘Usfan, and ‘Umar had appointed him over Mecca. He said: “Whom have you appointed over the people of the valley?” He said: “Ibn Abza.” He said: “Who is Ibn Abza?” He said: “A freedman of ours.” He said: “You appointed a freedman over them?!” He said: “He is a reciter of the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic, and he is knowledgeable of the inheritance laws.” ‘Umar said: “Indeed, your Prophet ﷺ said: ‘God raises some people by this Book and lowers others by it.’”
 Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (817:269).

٧٧٢٠ — عن زيد بن ثابت قال: أمرني رسول الله ﷺ فتعلمت له كتاب يهود، وقال: ((إني والله ما آمن يهود على كتابي)). فتعلمته، فلم يمر بي إلا نصف شهر حتى حذقته، فكنت أكتب له إذا كتب، وأقرأ له إذا كُتب إليه.
 حسن: رواه أبو داود (٣٦٤٥) — واللفظ له —، والترمذي (٢٧١٥)، وأحمد (٢١٦١٨)، وعلقه البخاري في الأحكام (٧١٩٥) عن خارجة بن زيد به مختصرًا. وقال الترمذي: حديث حسن صحيح.

7720 — Zayd ibn Thabit said: The Messenger of God ﷺ commanded me, so I learned for him the writing of the Jews. He said: “By God, I do not trust the Jews with my writing.” So I learned it, and only half a month passed before I mastered it. I used to write for him when he wrote, and read to him when something was written to him.
 Good: Narrated by Abu Dawud (3645), with his wording; al-Tirmidhi (2715); and Ahmad (21618). Al-Bukhari cited it in suspended form in the Book of Judgments (7195), from Kharijah ibn Zayd, in abridged form. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is a good authentic hadith.

٧٧٢١ — عن زيد بن ثابت قال: بعث إليَّ أبو بكر لمقتل أهل اليمامة، وعنده عمر، فقال أبو بكر: إن عمر أتاني فقال: إن القتل قد استحر يوم اليمامة بقراء القرآن، وإني أخشى أن يستحر القتل بقراء القرآن في المواطن كلها، فيذهب قرآن كثير، وإني أرى أن تأمر بجمع القرآن. قلت: كيف أفعل شيئًا لم يفعله رسول الله ﷺ؟ فقال عمر: هو والله خير. فلم يزل عمر يراجعني في ذلك حتى شرح الله صدري للذي شرح له صدر عمر، ورأيت في ذلك الذي رأى عمر.
 قال زيد: قال أبو بكر: وإنك رجل شاب عاقل لا نتهمك، قد كنت تكتب الوحي لرسول الله ﷺ، فتتبع القرآن فاجمعه. قال زيد: فوالله لو كلفني نقل جبل من الجبال ما كان بأثقل علي مما كلفني من جمع القرآن. قلت: كيف تفعلان شيئًا لم يفعله رسول الله ﷺ؟ قال أبو بكر: هو والله خير. فلم يزل أبو بكر يراجعني حتى شرح الله صدري للذي شرح الله له صدر أبي بكر وعمر، ورأيت في ذلك الذي رأيا. فتتبعت القرآن أجمعه من العُسُب، والرقاع، واللخاف، وصدور الرجال، فوجدت آخر سورة التوبة: (لَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ) [التوبة: ١٢٨] إلى آخرها مع خزيمة أو أبي خزيمة، فألحقتها في سورتها. وكانت الصحف عند أبي بكر حياته حتى توفاه الله عز وجل، ثم عند عمر حياته حتى توفاه الله، ثم عند حفصة بنت عمر.
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٧١٩١).

7721 — Zayd ibn Thabit said: Abu Bakr sent for me after the killing of the people of al-Yamamah, and ‘Umar was with him. Abu Bakr said: “‘Umar came to me and said: ‘The killing was severe among the reciters of the Qur’an on the day of al-Yamamah, and I fear that killing may become severe among the reciters of the Qur’an in all places, causing much of the Qur’an to be lost. I think you should order the collection of the Qur’an.’” I said: “How can I do something the Messenger of God ﷺ did not do?” ‘Umar said: “By God, it is good.” ‘Umar continued to discuss it with me until God opened my chest to what He had opened ‘Umar’s chest, and I saw in the matter what ‘Umar saw.
 Zayd said: Abu Bakr said: “You are a young, intelligent man whom we do not suspect. You used to write revelation for the Messenger of God ﷺ, so search for the Qur’an and collect it.” Zayd said: By God, if he had charged me with moving one of the mountains, it would not have been heavier upon me than what he charged me with regarding the collection of the Qur’an. I said: “How can you both do something that the Messenger of God ﷺ did not do?” Abu Bakr said: “By God, it is good.” Abu Bakr continued to discuss it with me until God opened my chest to what He had opened the chests of Abu Bakr and ‘Umar, and I saw in the matter what they saw. So I searched for the Qur’an, collecting it from palm stalks, parchments, flat stones, and the chests of men, until I found the end of the chapter of Repentance — “There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves” [Repentance: 128] to the end of it — with Khuzaymah or Abu Khuzaymah, so I placed it in its chapter. The written sheets remained with Abu Bakr during his life until God, Mighty and Majestic, took him in death, then with ‘Umar during his life until God took him in death, then with Hafsah bint ‘Umar.
 Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhari (7191).
